DistrictAttr: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum (Cultural), one of Vietnam's most iconic landmarks and a symbol of national identity. - A tribute to the life and legacy of Ho Chi Minh, the former president of North Vietnam. - 1969-1973 and 2010-present. - A grand marble mausoleum with two guard towers on each side, designed by Vo Nguyen Giap, a Vietnamese military leader and politician, in collaboration with other architects and designers from Vietnam. - The Mausoleum has been used as the final resting place of Ho Chi Minh since September 1973. - It is considered one of the most important symbols of national identity, and its architecture reflects the country's history, culture, and people. - Visitors to the mausoleum can see a statue of Ho Chi Minh lying in state in his tomb.
